To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the noise performance of JFETs fabricated in high-resistivity silicon can be significantly improved by means of a deep p-welling process.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of fabricating JFETs in a radiation detector technology, with noise performance comparable to that of the best available devices.
we have developed a new radiation-hardened silicon process for integrated circuits and that we have fabricated n-channel junction field effect transistors (JFETs) in this process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of low-noise devices for applications in radiation detection systems.
the design, the fabrication and the characterization of low noise junction field effect transistors in a silicon radiation detector technology.
the development of a new generation of low noise JFETs in the framework of an innovative radiation detector technology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the process is suitable for low noise applications and the noise figures are in good agreement with theoretical expectations.

, with respect to the previous devices, we have obtained: - an improvement of the noise figure by a factor of 3 to 4; - a better uniformity of the noise behavior; - an improved stability against radiation damage.
a new technology is being developed which is able to provide a very high quality read-out circuit in a radiation detector substrate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a noise performance of about 1.5 fA/√Hz has been obtained for transistors with a gate area as small as 1.5 x 10-4 μm2.
we have developed a radiation detector technology which allows the fabrication of low noise JFETs on a high resistivity substrate.
we have demonstrated the possibility of obtaining low noise JFETs in a standard detector technology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to obtain low noise devices with a standard process, with no special requirements on the substrate material.
a low noise performance is achievable in a radiation detector technology, with the potential of a significant impact on future applications.

it is possible to fabricate low noise transistors in a silicon detector technology and that these transistors can be used to implement charge sensitive amplifiers with noise performance comparable with that of commercial devices fabricated with dedicated technologies.
